title: Dzień dobry, mówi Tomasz Lewandowski
focus: phone calls and formal emails: set phrases and the conditional

lines.speaker: Sekretariat
lines.en: Institute of Linguistics, departmental office. Hello?

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.pl: Dzień dobry, mówi|mowi Tomasz Lewandowski. Czy mógłbym|moglbym rozmawiać z panią|pania_instr profesor Malinowską|malinowska?
lines.en: Good morning, this is Tomasz Lewandowski. Could I speak to Professor Malinowska?

lines.speaker: Sekretariat
lines.pl: Niestety, pani profesor jest dziś na konferencji|konferencji w Gdańsku|gdansku. Czy mogę coś przekazać|przekazac?
lines.en: I’m afraid the professor is at a conference in Gdańsk today. Can I take a message?

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.pl: Tak, bardzo proszę. Chodzi|chodzi o wykład|wyklad gościnny, o którym|ktorym rozmawialiśmy|rozmawialismy w zeszłym tygodniu.
lines.en: Yes, please. It’s about the guest lecture we discussed last week.

lines.speaker: Sekretariat
lines.pl: Rozumiem. Czy pani profesor ma pana|pana_gen numer?
lines.en: I see. Does the professor have your number?

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.pl: Chyba nie. To sześćset dwa, czterysta trzynaście, osiemset siedem. Byłbym|bylbym wdzięczny|wdzieczny, gdyby|gdyby pani profesor oddzwoniła|oddzwonila po powrocie|powrocie.
lines.en: I don’t think so. It’s 602 413 807. I’d be grateful if the professor could call me back when she returns.

lines.speaker: Sekretariat
lines.pl: Oczywiście, przekażę|przekaze. Proponuję|proponuje też napisać do niej|niej maila|maila, bo na pewno sprawdza pocztę|poczte.
lines.en: Of course, I’ll pass it on. I’d also suggest emailing her, because she’ll certainly be checking her mail.

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.pl: Dziękuję bardzo, tak zrobię. Do usłyszenia|uslyszenia!
lines.en: Thank you very much, I’ll do that. Goodbye!

lines.speaker: Tomek (e-mail)
lines.pl: Szanowna|szanowna Pani|pani_letter Profesor|profesor_letter, nawiązując|nawiazujac do naszej rozmowy w Krakowie, chciałbym|chcialbym serdecznie zaprosić Panią|pania_letter do wygłoszenia|wygloszenia wykładu|wykladu gościnnego|goscinnego.
lines.en: Dear Professor Malinowska, following up on our conversation in Kraków, I would like to warmly invite you to give a guest lecture.

jezykoznawstwa.why: Instytut Językoznawstwa, “Institute of Linguistics”: the second noun is in the genitive. Compare językoznawczyni in the previous lesson: same roots, different suffix.

slucham.why: Answering the phone, Poles often say słucham, “I’m listening.” In a shop or office it means “how can I help?”, and with rising intonation, “pardon?”

parts: verb stem; 3rd sg. has no ending
mowi.why: On the phone you introduce yourself in the third person: mówi Tomasz Lewandowski, “Tomasz Lewandowski speaking.” Z tej strony Tomasz Lewandowski is also common.

moglbym.tags: verb · imperfective · conditional · 1st person singular · masculine
moglbym.why: Czy mógłbym…? is the standard polite request, “could I…?” It’s masculine, with no agreement ending, because Tomek is the speaker.

you.f: You would say: Czy mogłabym…? (ó becomes o before -a).

parts: instr. sg. -ą (the i marks soft ń)
pania_instr.why: Rozmawiać z + instrumental: z panią profesor. Pani has the same form, panią, in the accusative and the instrumental. Profesor stays undeclined, because it refers to a woman.

malinowska.why: Feminine surnames in -ska decline like adjectives: Malinowska, Malinowskiej, Malinowską. Here it’s instrumental after z.

konferencji.why: Na + locative for events: na konferencji, na koncercie, na weselu. Towns and buildings usually take w: w Gdańsku.

gdansku.tags: proper noun · masculine inanimate · locative singular
gdansku.why: W + locative. Stems ending in k take -u: w Gdańsku, w roku, w bloku.

przekazac.why: Czy mogę coś przekazać? is the standard “can I take a message?” Prze- here means passing something on from one person to another.

chodzi.tags: verb · imperfective · present · 3rd person singular · impersonal use
parts: verb stem; 3rd sg. has no ending
chodzi.why: Chodzi o + accusative means “it’s about, it concerns.” The motion verb chodzić is used impersonally here, with no subject. Chodzi mi o to, że… means “What I mean is…”

wyklad.tags: noun · masculine inanimate · accusative singular (same as nominative)
wyklad.why: O + accusative after chodzi. Masculine inanimate nouns usually look the same in the accusative as in the nominative.
wyklad.history: From wykładać, “to lay out”: a lecture sets out its subject.

ktorym.why: Który takes its gender from the noun it refers to (wykład, masculine) and its case from its own clause: rozmawiać o + locative, so o którym.

rozmawialismy.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 1st person plural · virile
rozmawialismy.why: “We” is Tomek and the professor, and one man makes the group virile, so the ending is -i. Before it, ł is written l.

you.f: With a mixed group: rozmawialiśmy. Only women: rozmawiałyśmy.

pana_gen.tags: formal pronoun · masculine · genitive singular, used as a possessive
pana_gen.why: The formal “your” is the genitive of pan or pani, placed before the noun: pana numer, pani numer. It doesn’t change with the noun’s case: z pana numerem.

you.m: Asked about your number: pana numer.
you.f: Asked about your number: pani numer.

bylbym.why: Byłbym wdzięczny, gdyby…, “I’d be grateful if…”, is the standard formula for a polite request, in speech and in writing.

wdzieczny.why: The adjective agrees with the speaker: wdzięczny for a man, wdzięczna for a woman.

gdyby.why: With a third-person subject, gdyby takes no person marker and the verb is a bare past form: gdyby pani profesor oddzwoniła.

oddzwonila.tags: verb · perfective · past form · 3rd person singular · feminine
oddzwonila.why: Od- here means “back, in response”: oddzwonić, odpisać (“write back”), oddać (“give back”). Feminine to agree with pani profesor.

parts: t → ć before loc. -e, spelled ci
powrocie.why: Po + locative means “after”: po powrocie, po obiedzie. Before the locative ending, ó becomes o and t softens to ć: powrót → powrocie.
powrocie.compare: Po + accusative means “to fetch”: iść po chleb.

przekaze.tags: verb · perfective · non-past (future meaning) · 1st person singular
przekaze.why: Perfective, so the present form refers to the future: “I’ll pass it on.” The z of przekazać alternates with ż in the present: przekażę, przekażesz.

proponuje.why: Proponuję + infinitive, “I suggest (doing)”, is a polite way to recommend something.

niej.tags: pronoun · genitive · form used after a preposition
niej.why: After a preposition, third-person pronouns take an initial n-: jej → do niej, jego → dla niego, im → z nimi.

maila.tags: noun · masculine inanimate · accusative singular (genitive-like form)
parts: acc. sg. -a, as in the genitive
maila.why: Masculine inanimate nouns usually have an accusative identical to the nominative, but a number of everyday nouns take -a: napisać maila, wysłać SMS-a, zjeść banana. Napisać mail is also correct.

poczte.why: Poczta means both “post office” and “mail.” Sprawdzać pocztę is the usual way to say “check one’s email.”

uslyszenia.why: Do usłyszenia, “until we hear (each other)”, is the phone counterpart of do widzenia, “until we see (each other)”. Do takes the genitive.

szanowna.why: Szanowna Pani / Szanowny Panie is the standard formal opening of a letter or email, the equivalent of “Dear …”. A title usually follows, without the surname: Szanowna Pani Profesor.
szanowna.compare: To a man: Szanowny Panie Profesorze.

pani_letter.why: In letters and emails, Pan, Pani and Państwo are capitalised as a mark of respect, in all their forms: Pani, Panią, Pana. The dialogue lines above are speech, so they’re written in lower case.

profesor_letter.tags: noun · not declined when referring to a woman
profesor_letter.why: Capitalised in the salutation along with Pani. As in speech, it doesn’t decline when it refers to a woman.

nawiazujac.gloss: to refer to, follow up on
nawiazujac.why: Nawiązując do…, “following up on…”, is a fixed opening in formal letters. The -ąc form means “while doing” and must have the same subject as the main verb, here Tomek.
nawiazujac.history: Literally “tying on to”: wiązać means “to tie.”

chcialbym.tags: verb · imperfective · conditional · 1st person singular · masculine
chcialbym.why: In formal writing, the conditional chciałbym is the usual way to state an intention or request.

pania_letter.tags: formal pronoun · feminine · accusative singular · capitalised in letters
parts: acc. sg. -ą (the i marks soft ń)
pania_letter.why: Zaprosić kogoś: the person invited is in the accusative. Capitalised because this is a letter.

wygloszenia.why: Zaprosić kogoś do + genitive: to invite someone to do something. Formal Polish often uses a verbal noun where English uses a verb: do wygłoszenia wykładu, “to give a lecture.”

wykladu.why: Genitive after the verbal noun: wygłoszenie wykładu, “the delivery of a lecture.”

goscinnego.why: Wykład gościnny is a guest lecture. The adjective comes after the noun, as it usually does when the phrase names a type of thing.

wyrazami.why: Z wyrazami szacunku, “with expressions of respect”, is the standard formal sign-off, roughly “Yours sincerely.” Z poważaniem is also formal, if a little official; Pozdrawiam is less formal.

szacunku.why: Genitive after wyrazami: “expressions of respect.” The e of szacunek is fleeting, as in Rynek → Rynku.

exercises.prompt: Ask on the phone: “Could I speak to Mr. Nowak?” Czy ___ rozmawiać z panem Nowakiem?

explain.m: móg + ł + by + m: the ó stays in the closed syllable.
explain.f: mog + ł + a + by + m: with -a after it, the syllable opens and ó becomes o.

exercises.hint: Check the learner setting at the top, and remember mógł → mogła.

exercises.prompt: “If Mr. Nowak called back…” Gdyby pan Nowak ___ (oddzwonić)
exercises.explain: After gdyby, a third-person subject takes the bare past form; masculine has no agreement ending: od + dzwoni + ł.
exercises.hint: Compare gdyby pani profesor oddzwoniła. What changes for a man?

exercises.explain: After a preposition, jego becomes niego: n + iego.
exercises.hint: Compare do niej: what was added to jej?

exercises.prompt: Open an email to a male professor: ___ Panie Profesorze,
exercises.explain: The adjective agrees with Panie, which is masculine: Szanowny Panie Profesorze.
exercises.hint: Szanowna agrees with Pani. Which ending goes with Panie?

exercises.explain: Po meaning “after” takes the locative. The stem changes, a → e and d → dź (spelled dzi): obiad → obiedzie.
exercises.hint: Look at po powrocie, then think of miasto → mieście.
